input_contract.preservation: Exact source tokens, their order and single separating spaces are preserved. Paragraph breaks are explicit reset boundaries; ordinary physical line wraps do not reset. Capitalization and listed punctuation are preserved. Repeated whitespace and exact original lineation are outside this canonical input contract. An unlisted character is an explicit coverage failure, never silently normalized or dropped.
input_contract.unknown_words: There is no lexical dictionary. Every new word over the declared character inventory is handled by exactly the same per-character rules. No ingredient, action, scope, comparison, pronoun or negation is replaced by a semantic label.
input_contract.rare_encoding: For zero-based index j in additional_characters_in_order, write y, then working_glyphs[floor(j/22)], then working_glyphs[j mod22]. All three marks form one character. Reject unused indices. Rare characters do not update the ordinary-letter state.
input_contract.meanings: The shapes are familiar working transcription labels used for an artificial demonstration. This is not a native atomic inventory, source-language identification or Voynich sound/word assignment.

common_readability: A decoder reads code units inside each visible source-word group and reproduces every input character. It starts from the public paragraph initialization and updates only from previously decoded characters. No source plaintext, per-message side table or private identifier is needed. Random access to a middle word without earlier paragraph state is not promised.

title: RAW UNREVIEWED: a movable26-letter strip writes current rank then moves the letter to the front
summary: A writer keeps a26-letter strip in a public initial order, writes the current position of each source letter and moves that letter to the front. A reader performs the same small list operation on recovered letters. This transmits arbitrary ordinary words without a learned word inventory or a stored whole-text history.

design.purpose: A complete source-forward rank notation whose changing alphabet is generated by a concrete movable letter strip, rather than trained context tables or503-word lookup.
design.initialization: At paragraph start the movable list is the ordinary alphabet a through z. Carry the list across words and ordinary line wraps; reset only at explicit paragraph boundaries.

rank_carrier.mapping: Ranks0..19 use the20 direct signs in the listed order. Ranks20..25 use q followed by working_glyphs[rank-20]. The common y plus two-selector branch carries additional characters. Reject all other q selectors and unused rare indices.
rank_carrier.unit_boundaries: q consumes exactly one following selector, y consumes exactly two, and every other initial drawing is a one-sign rank unit. Parsing never needs an unseen source letter.

encode: For a lowercase letter, find its current zero-based position k in the26-letter list, emit rank k, remove the letter from that position and insert it at position0, preserving the relative order of all others.
A listed additional character uses the y escape and leaves the list unchanged. Preserve source spaces and paragraph breaks exactly under the declared input contract.
decode: Parse a rank unit, select the letter currently at that rank, emit it, and perform the identical move-to-front update.
A rare-character unit emits that exact character without list change. The next rank therefore depends only on the reader's own recovered text, never an external plaintext oracle.
design.learning_and_operation: The reader learns26 rank codes plus the fixed56-character auxiliary table and keeps26 movable letter entries. The state space is26! possible orders, not26 states, but no26!-entry table is learned. A naive hand operation may search or shift up to26 letters for each character; a strip/table is required and practicality is unproven.
design.single_and_repeated_inputs: Any single letter and unfamiliar word are legal. Immediately repeated lowercase letters use rank0 after the first occurrence. Repeated whole words are written in full; no pointer substitutes for a word.
design.exact_unequal_consequence: Two source letters' relative order changes only when one of them is used. An immediately repeated lowercase letter necessarily has rank0. For a fixed source word repeated consecutively, the list after its first occurrence is a fixed point for further occurrences of that word; thus the second and third encoded whole-word forms must be identical.
design.proof_scope: Writing a fixed word moves precisely its lowercase letters to the front, ordered by their last occurrence in that word; untouched letters retain their prior relative order. Repeating the same word produces the same resulting list. This formal argument uses no corpus.
design.strongest_countercase: A run of one repeated source letter becomes a run of the same rank0 drawing after its first letter. The mechanism can concentrate repetitions instead of dispersing them. Repeated whole words stabilize after one occurrence, so it does not offer unrestricted context-dependent variants. An error can disturb all subsequent ranks until reset.
design.smallest_falsifier: A consecutive repeated source letter requiring a nonzero second rank, or different second/third forms for an unchanged word repeated three times without reset, contradicts the fixed lesson. Also reject any decoder that obtains its list from supplied plaintext rather than the output it has already recovered.
design.cost_limit: Ordinary characters cost one or two signs and additional characters three, but one potentially costly list manipulation is required per ordinary character. No writing-time measurement or inherited-statistic pass is claimed.
design.predecessors: GDT1179 C used nearest prior whole-word distance and a503-word history. This uses only the recency ordering of26 ordinary letters, with no word-index meanings. GDT001 native inverse failures and the closed exact-root-recency family are not reopened; root-level recency is a different observable from this unbound source-letter construction.
